title: Ask for a Simpler Explanation
subtitle: Learn how to get clear instructions and truly understand them.
objectives: Ask for simpler words, one step at a time, or a different example.
Compare a simpler version with the original rules to check for missing details.
Explain rules back in your own words to confirm understanding.

scenes.title: Confusing Rules?
scenes.display: Game Rules: Place MOON first, STAR last. SUN must be between them. Explain your order in one sentence.
scenes.narration: Ever read confusing instructions, like complex game rules? They seem simple, but their meaning can be unclear. Let's learn to get clearer explanations.
scenes.visualAction: A character looks confused at a complex set of game rules on a screen. Three cards (SUN, MOON, STAR) appear on screen, then shuffle randomly.

scenes.title: Why Ask for Simpler?
scenes.display: Ask for: Simpler words, One step at a time, A different example.
scenes.narration: Instructions often use big words or many ideas. It's fine to ask for help! Request simpler words, a breakdown, or another example. This clarifies the main point.
scenes.visualAction: A character points to a thought bubble with 'Simpler words?' 'Step-by-step?' 'Another example?' icons. The confusing rules from the hook scene transform into a list of these three options.

scenes.title: Checking for Accuracy
scenes.display: Original vs. Simple: Does the meaning stay the same?
scenes.narration: When you get a simpler explanation, compare it to the original. Was anything missed? Does it still mean the same? We want simpler, not incomplete!
scenes.visualAction: Two versions of the game rules appear side-by-side: the original and a simplified version. A magnifying glass icon moves between them, highlighting differences or similarities.

scenes.title: Your Own Words
scenes.display: Explain it back in your own words.
scenes.narration: Explain the rules back in your own words, then compare with the original. This can reveal gaps. Clear wording alone does not prove every detail is correct.
scenes.visualAction: A character gestures towards a speech bubble with an 'Explain it!' icon. The three cards (SUN, MOON, STAR) are shown correctly ordered according to the rules, then a character nods in understanding.

scenes.title: Better Questions
scenes.display: Initial: 'What does this mean?' Improved: 'Can you explain 'between them' using another example?'
scenes.narration: Asking 'What does this mean?' is a start. Specific questions lead to better answers. Ask about a word, phrase, or request a different example. Be precise!
scenes.visualAction: A character types 'What does this mean?' into a chat bubble, then deletes it. They then type 'Can you explain 'between them' using another example?' and a lightbulb appears above their head.

scenes.title: Let's Practice!
scenes.display: Activity: Simplify instructions for a short task.
scenes.narration: Now it's your turn! I'll give you short instructions. Ask for a simpler explanation, then write the rules in your own words. Check your version carefully.
scenes.visualAction: A character presents a scroll with new, short instructions. A pencil and notebook icon appears, prompting the learner to start writing.

scenes.title: You're a Pro!
scenes.display: You can ask for clearer explanations and truly understand them!
scenes.narration: Great job! You learned to ask for clear explanations, check accuracy, and explain them. This skill helps understand all instructions, from games to schoolwork!
scenes.visualAction: A character gives a thumbs-up. The three cards (SUN, MOON, STAR) are shown in their correct order, then a checkmark appears over them.

reading.title: Getting Clearer
reading.text: When instructions are confusing, don't guess! Ask for simpler words, one step at a time, or a different example. This helps you understand the core idea without getting lost in complex language. Always compare the simpler version to the original to make sure nothing was missed.

reading.title: The Card Game Rules
reading.text:
You have 3 imaginary cards: SUN, MOON and STAR. Place MOON first and STAR last, with SUN between them. Explain your order in one sentence.
Start with MOON. Put SUN next. Make STAR the last card. Write one sentence explaining the order.

reading.title: Confirming Understanding
reading.text: Explain the rules in your own words, then compare your explanation with the original. Clear wording can help reveal gaps; it does not prove that every detail is correct.

promptExamples.initial: I don't get the card game rules. What do I do?
promptExamples.improved: Simplify these instructions into short steps while keeping every requirement.
promptExamples.followup: The incomplete version leaves out STAR. Add its position and keep the one-sentence explanation requirement.

activity.title: Simpler words, same rules
activity.instructions: Write a request for simpler wording, then explain the rules in your own words. Compare your version with the original and mark each of the four requirements you kept.
activity.starter: You have 3 imaginary cards: SUN, MOON and STAR. Place MOON first and STAR last, with SUN between them. Explain your order in one sentence.
activity.expectedEvidence: A simplification request, your own explanation, and a check of all four requirements.

quiz.question: What is the best way to check if a simpler explanation is accurate?
options: Trust the person who gave you the simpler explanation.
Compare the simpler version with the original rules.
Just try to follow the simpler instructions right away.
quiz.explanation: Comparing the simpler version with the original rules helps you catch any missing details or changes in meaning. It's good to trust, but better to verify!

quiz.question: You're playing the card game from the lesson. You arrange the cards as STAR, SUN, MOON. Which rule did you miss?
options: Explain your order in one sentence.
Place MOON first and STAR last.
quiz.explanation: The original rules clearly state 'Place MOON first and STAR last.' In the order STAR, SUN, MOON, this combined rule is entirely missed, as MOON is not first and STAR is not last. While SUN is between them, and you could explain your order, the primary rule about the placement of MOON and STAR is violated.

quiz.question: Which requirement is missing from the incomplete version in the lesson materials?
options: Explain the order in one sentence.
quiz.explanation: The incomplete version mentions MOON and asks for one sentence, but omits STAR and its position. Compare it with the original to restore the requirement.

mission.title: An imaginary reading-club notice
mission.instructions: These are invented instructions for a notice: 'Put the title at the top, two sentences about the reading club below it, and 3 invented book titles at the bottom. Check the sheet before displaying it.' Write a request to simplify these instructions. Then explain them in your own words while keeping all four requirements.
rubric: I wrote a clear request for simpler wording.
I kept the title position and two-sentence requirement.
I kept the 3 invented book titles.
I kept the checking step and used my own wording.

hints.question: What if I don't know what part of the instructions to ask about?
hints.answer: Read the instructions slowly. Circle any words you don't know, or any sentences that seem to have too many ideas at once. Those are good places to start asking for simpler words or a step-by-step breakdown.

hints.question: How can I make sure my simpler explanation isn't missing anything?
hints.answer: Look at each original rule one by one. Does your simpler version still include that exact rule? For example, if the original says 'MOON first,' does your simpler version also say 'MOON first' or something that means the same thing?

hints.question: What if I explain it back, but I'm still wrong?
hints.answer: That's okay! It means you're still learning. Ask the person who explained it to you to point out exactly where your explanation went wrong. Then, try to explain that part again until you get it right.

educatorNotes.sampleAnswer:
Activity: Start with MOON. Put SUN next. Make STAR the last card. Write one sentence explaining the order.
Mission: title at the top; two sentences below; three invented book titles at the bottom; check before display.
educatorNotes.commonMisconception: A common misconception is that 'simpler' means 'shorter' or 'less detailed.' Students might accidentally remove important constraints or details when trying to simplify, leading to an incomplete understanding. Emphasize that all original rules must be preserved.
